concepts.why: The patient presents with a painless right vulvar mass extending into the right inguinal region, which is consistent with a Canal of Nuck hernia, and ultrasound findings show a well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass tracking into the inguinal canal.

The patient's non-tender mass of the right labia majora could be a lipoma, which is a common benign tumor of the vulva, and the ultrasound findings of a well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass are consistent with this diagnosis.

The patient's mass could be a Bartholin gland cyst, which is a common cause of a vulvar mass, and the ultrasound findings of a well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass with mild peripheral blood flow are consistent with this diagnosis.

The patient's non-tender mass of the right labia majora could be a fibroma, which is a benign tumor of the vulva, and the ultrasound findings of a well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass are consistent with this diagnosis.
